answer: Each identity grows as a living vine: every epoch it grafts one new branch of verified work, sealed in a fourteen-line sonnet signed by a distinct peer who checked it. A beacon flashes at random and lights one branch per vine for a pruning audit, where reviewers inspect the graft and its sonnet for copies. A failed audit prunes the branch, slashes the vine's standing, and forces regrowth. Running many fake vines means producing distinct peer-signed sonnets and real work for each, every epoch, under unpredictable audits — a cost scaling with every identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
